newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Oil slips as Iraq oil sale concerns dispelled.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Oil slips as Iraq oil sale concerns dispelled.

text.p: World oil prices retreated on Friday as concerns were calmed that Iraqi oil sales under a United Nations programme might be in jeopardy.
International bellwether North Sea Brent blend for June delivery slipped 16 cents a barrel to trade at $18.25 at 1534 GMT.
Oil has settled in a tight range around $18 after a three-month $7 slide took Brent to a 10-month low at $17.54 in early April.
Prices slipped a little on Friday after the United Nations denied a report carried by the BBC on Thursday that six U.N. oil sale monitors had gone missing in northern Iraq.

Traders had taken fright at the report, sourced from the Iraqi opposition group the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan, and accusing a rival Kurdish group, the Kurdistan Democratic Party, of arresting the six.
Iraq is on target to sell a permitted $2 billion worth of crude over a six-month period by early June under the U.N. exchange.
Dealers expect the $2 billion sale to be renewed for a second six months.
Analysts said they saw little chance of it being called off.
"I'm advising my clients the deal will be renewed. I see very little likelihood it would be called off," one London-based oil analyst said.
Oil dealers said crude prices continued to find support from healthy refining margins which although down in recent days still are higher than last year's average.
But some said a huge heating oil and diesel buying spree by Singapore trading house Hin Leong, which has underpinned global refining margins in recent weeks, looked to have run its course.
Hin Leong was seeking to capture a big share of the lucrative Chinese diesel market, traders said.
They said the company was responsible for purchases of around 17 million barrels since early March worth about $500 million.
